name: Rick Rubin
sources: The Ringer — the magic of Rick Rubin is in what he doesn't do (https://www.theringer.com/2020/06/25/music/rick-rubin-producer-legacy-def-jam-shangri-la)
notes: Windowed to the documented 1994+ reduction era only, per the research's era gate — this is not the 1980s Def Jam entry and should not be read as one. "Subtraction is the method" is the whole model: a single loud rock break rather than a layered kit, so `velocityTiers` runs [96,112] on main hits (the loudest here) while `percs.lanes` is emptied entirely and every ornament probability is at or near its floor. The harmony is blues-derived and carried by a guitar figure with no pads — `extensions.triad` at 0.85 is the highest on this axis and ninths are 0.02 — over a blues and minor-pentatonic scale set that nothing else here uses. "Extreme low note density" is [1,3] notes a bar with `emptyBarBias` 0.28 and a guitar-range melody starting at 52, the lowest register on this axis. ⚠ **Two engine floors are visible and both are named rather than hidden.** The research says "no hats at all on the signature rap record": a model that declares a hat block must produce hats on every seed, so `continuous` is false at the 0.28 `fillDensity` floor with the velocities pulled to [0.35,0.55] — as close to absent as this engine reaches. And the research says "no fills"; 8/16 is the sparsest the fill grammar goes. ⚠ The bass is `mirror_kick` at `followRootsProb` 0.97 with no glide and no passing tones, which is the research's "single-note electric bass on the root" — the "often no bass at all" half is not expressible, since the part is always generated. ⚠ `medium`, matching the research's "medium-high for the era-windowed claims": the reductive philosophy is well documented but the technical detail is journalism rather than gear interviews. The specific inferred parameter is `session.humanize.quantizeStrength` at 0.72, this author's reading of "a single played rock break". ⚠ **The bass pool was widened after `bass.rs` measured it at 0.946 distinct against a floor of 0.95.** It was authored with NO passing tones, followRootsProb 0.97, anticipationProb 0.05 over register [28,45] — a faithful description of a sample-loop bass, and one that leaves a seed nothing to vary but root and octave. Now ["P5"], root lock 0.9, anticipation 0.18, register [28,47]. The line is still overwhelmingly root-on-kick; what changed is how many different records it can be, not how busy any one of them is. ⚠ The chord voicing moved up to [48, 82] so the bass stays under the harmony — it started at 40 against a bass reaching 47, an overlap of 8. The span is preserved; a voicing that low was competing with the bass rather than sitting over it. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 627 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: styles 3, densityRatio 0.5, melody density [1,5]. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [1,2], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 947/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980**, so its style pool was opened: bell_echo, densityRatio 0.55. ⛔ `counter.rs` reads five styles and this roster only ever authored three — `bell_echo` is a real answer shape the engine can already play and the dataset had never asked for. ⚠ `sustain_pad` is deliberately not added: it is a held pad rather than an answer, and adding one to win a variety score would change what the record sounds like. ⚠ **The melody floor was raised from [1,5] to [2,6] because the COUNTERMELODY was saturating at 945/1000 against a floor of 980.** The counter answers inside the lead: a melody allowed to thin to a single note a bar leaves it almost nothing to answer, and no amount of counter styles or density can recover what the lead never played. This is the lead becoming reliably present, not busier — the upper bound is what carries the density and it is unchanged where it was already 6 or more. ⚠ **`melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.28 to 0.1, and this is the parameter that was actually saturating the countermelody** (this model reached 945/1000 against a floor of 980). An empty bar produces an empty counter region, and every empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one — so silence is the one thing a seed cannot vary. Across the roster 57 of the 58 models failing this gate authored an empty-bar bias, averaging 0.246, against 0.115 for the models that passed. The space in the lead is real and is kept; what is removed is the amount of it that made every take collide.
